BILL NUMBER: S1443

SPONSOR: ADDABBO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and breeding law, in
relation to state gaming commission occupational licenses

 
PURPOSE:  Relates to licensing of commercial casinos employees and
vendors of commercial casinos

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section a: Adding New Section 104-a Streamlines the Commission's licens-
ing processes and creates one univeral "Gaming Commission Registration"
that all applicants will file and then eachò applicant can apply. for
what will then be considered sub-licenses or sub-registrations "under"
their Commission Registration. It authorities the Commission to exchange
fingerprint data with and receive criminal history record state and
federal law enforcement agencies. This section authorizes the Commission
to promulgate rules and regulations.

Section 2: Adds section of 31-a, defining a non-gaming employee.

Section 3: Expands the disqualification of certain applicants for licen-
sure.

Section 4: Authorizes the Commission to suspend a license pending an
investigation.

Section 5: Removes the automatic disqualification of an applicant for a
key gaming license, and maintains the discretion of the Commission to
deny or issue such license.

Section 6: Clarifies the progress of disqualifying an applicant for
licensure.

Section 7: Adds non-craning employees registrations to the statute. in
addition, divas the Commission the discretion to consider: a regis-
trant's rehabilitation pursuant to Article twenty-three-A of tin:
corrections when evaluating their application for licensure.  This
section outlines the Information and documentation an applicant must
submit for consideration.

Section 8 Provides the Commission discretion to conduct a. background
investigation into the qualification of an applicant the Commission, Ii
still receive fingerprints and an application to evaluate It will be
discretionary for non-gaming registrations, if they need to be sent for
a further investigation.

This section also provides that the granting of a. gaming license or
gaming registration shall apply only to the job title listed in the
application; the Commission mar, upon request, allow the transfer of
said license or registration to another job title. This section adds.
non-gaming to reflect current practice. Provides the Commission the
discretion to suspend, revoke or limit an employee's license or regis-
tration if it 4s determined that the employee is no longer qualified to
hold such license or registration.

Section 9: Clarifies the definition and classification of vendors
providing goods and services to a gaming facility. Provides the Commis-
sion with the discretion to change the level of ii censure of a vendor
based upon the business conducted in a specific time period.

Section 10: Provides that employees of vendors must qualify' for lice-
sure under standards established by the Commission. Harmonizes the stan-
dard of licensure required for vendor employees and casino employees.

Section 11: Exempts any non-gaming vendor providing goods or service
valued at less than twenty-five thousand dollars in a twelve-month peri-
od from licensing requirements. However, the 'gaming facility shall
notify the Commission of such vendors.

Section 12 : Cleans up the statutory language for consistency and ensur-
ing that Article 23A of the corrections law is consistently applied

Section 13: Provides the Gaming Commission with the discretion to waive
any of the requirements for licensure at she request of a gaming facili-
ty.

Section 14: Shall take effect immediately

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Streamlines the registration and licensure process for employees and
vendors and removes the absolute disqualification. of certain applicants
while maintaining the discretion of the Commission. This bill will also
recluse or eliminate burdensome requirements on small businesses
attempting to transact with a gaming facility.  The bill will also align
the license and registration. requirements of vendor employees with the
requirements placed on direct employees of the gaming facilities.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019: PASSED THE SENATE

2020: REFERRED TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Not Applicable.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

SPONSOR: ADDABBO

An act to amend the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and breeding law, in
relation to state gaming commission occupational licenses

 
PURPOSE:

Relates to licensing of commercial casinos employees and vendors of
commercial casinos

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Removes the automatic disqualification of an applicant for a
gaming facility or key employee license based on prior conviction of a
felony that does not involve public integrity, embezzlement, theft,
fraud or perjury.

Section 2: Removes the automatic disqualification of an applicant for a
key gaming license, and maintains the discretion of the Commission to
deny or issue such license.

Section 3: Exempts any non-gaming vendor providing goods or service
valued at less than twenty-five thousand dollars in a twelve-month peri-
od from licensing requirements.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Removes the absolute disqualification of certain applicants while main-
taining the discretion of the Commission. This bill will also reduce or
eliminate burdensome requirements on small businesses attempting to
transact with a gaming facility.

2020: REFERRED TO RACING, GAMING AND WAGERING

Not Applicable.

Immediately.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 105
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 1443-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the racing, pari-mutuel wagering and breeding law,
      in relation to state gaming commission occupational licenses"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  The current law in New York creates an automatic bar  to  receiving  a
casino  key  employee  license  for  any  person who has previously been
convicted of certain  enumerated  crimes.  This  bill  would  create  an
exemption to that prohibition.
 
  Employees  of  a  gaming  facility  are  engaged in sensitive jobs and
handle large amounts of money; this is particularly true  for  employees
who  hold  a  key  license. While I share the sponsors' desire to ensure
there are sufficient applicants for jobs at these facilities, I  believe
the current statutory scheme, including the safeguards relating to casi-
no key license eligibility, remains appropriate.
 
  Therefore, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
